title: Incident synthesis + secrets review — April 20 2026
content:
Meeting: Security Engineering sync — Incident synthesis and secrets review
Date: 2026-04-20
Facilitator: Asha Patel
Attendees: Asha P., Michael C., Sofia R., Jonah K., Priya N., (recording available on Slack thread)
Duration: 45m

Purpose:
- Combine recent triage findings into a short synthesis to drive prioritized remediation.
- Reconcile secrets scanner results with ongoing infra changes and decide short-term mitigations.
- Capture threat-model updates for the q2 infra rollout.

Agenda:
1) Quick status: open vulnerabilities and recent escalations (10m)
2) Secrets scanner summary and false-positive triage (10m)
3) Threat-model adjustments for sidecar auth change (10m)
4) Action items and owners (10m)
5) Parking lot / blockers (5m)

---
1) Status: open vulnerabilities 
Summary: We have three prioritized findings from last week’s automated scans plus one externally-reported issue. High-level notes: 
- SEC-1987 (external report): Privilege escalation pattern in telemetry ingest pipeline. Impact: potential lateral access to staging-only KV namespace. Current state: reproducer validated by Sofia, PoC limited to staging; not observed in prod. Immediate mitigation: rotated staging service account keys, pinned ingress rule to a narrower CIDR.
- INFRA-6421 (internal scan): Old package in image-builder container (glibc CVE-like). Impact: moderate; affects build images used by Dedicated fleet. Current state: fix in PR (infra#412) to move to base image with patched packages; rolling image rebuild queued.
- SEC-2012 (dependency alert): token parsing library flagged for DoS regex. Impact: low; library is behind rate limits. Decision: track, escalate if we shift parsing code to public endpoints.

Notes from discussion:
- We need a short “staging vs prod exposure” checklist for every externally-reported finding; Sofia will draft (Action A1).
- For SEC-1987, do an abbreviated postmortem if we see any evidence of cross-env access in logs (Action A2).

2) Secrets scanner: aggregated findings and false-positive triage
Summary: After running the updated scanner across mono-repo and infra repo, we have ~28 hits; after heuristics and quick triage we estimate ~6 actionable secrets. Many hits are k8s manifests with templated placeholders (false positives).
Key hits: 
- service-account API key found in a cache layer (path: infra/legacy/cache/credentials.json) — flagged as medium. Owner: Jonah. Immediate step: rotate the key and replace with KMS-backed secret (Action A3).
- hard-coded SaaS test token in a test fixture (path: pkg/x/test_fixtures/saas_token.test) — low impact. Plan: remove and replace with fake token generator (Action A4).
- AWS temp creds accidentally checked into a fork — rotated by security and flagged closed (done).

Triaging heuristics used (quick primer):
- Check if hit is within test/fixtures or template directory 
- Check token age and last use via audit logs
- Correlate with running resources (is the credential referenced by a running pod?)

Decisions:
- Adopt the relaxed heuristic set for baseline scanning to reduce noise, but mark heuristics in the scanner config as auditable changes (Sofia to open PR to scanner config; Action A5).
- Add a gating check in CI for infra/* that fails the pipeline if new secrets are committed to main (Jonah to add; Action A6).

3) Threat modeling: proposed adjustments tied to sidecar auth change
Context: Platform is moving to a sidecar-based auth proxy for internal service-to-service calls in Q2 rollout. This changes trust boundaries and credential lifetimes.
Threat-model notes: 
- New threat: sidecar compromise may allow token replay across internal services. Mitigations discussed: short-lived mTLS certs for sidecars, mutual attestation using instance identity, and strict ingress policies.
- Observation: caching layer (the same one with the flagged service-account) increases blast radius if sidecar can access cached credentials. We need to ensure sidecar has least privilege and cannot read persistent secrets.

Actionable recommendations to feed design:
- Enforce per-sidecar IAM roles with narrowly scoped permissions instead of node-level credentials (Action A7).
- Prototype ephemeral credential issuance via the internal token service (Priya taking lead; Action A8).
- Update threat-model doc with a new diagram and attack paths showing sidecar as a boundary (Asha to update Confluence; Action A9).

4) Action items (owner — due)
A1: Staging vs Prod exposure checklist draft — Sofia Ramirez — due 2026-04-23
A2: Abbreviated postmortem template for SEC-1987 if cross-env evidence found — Sofia Ramirez — due 2026-04-25
A3: Rotate cache service-account key and move to KMS-backed workflow — Jonah Kline — due 2026-04-22 (in progress)
A4: Remove hard-coded SaaS test token and create fake-generator helper — Michael Chen — due 2026-04-24
A5: PR to scanner heuristics to reduce noise and add audit note — Sofia Ramirez — due 2026-04-26
A6: CI gating for infra/* to block secrets on main — Jonah Kline — due 2026-04-28
A7: Enforce per-sidecar IAM roles design doc — Asha Patel + Platform Eng reviewer — draft due 2026-05-03
A8: Prototype ephemeral credential issuance (token-service integration) — Priya Natarajan — spike due 2026-05-07
A9: Update threat-model diagrams and attack paths — Asha Patel — due 2026-04-30

5) Parking lot / blockers:
- Need compute time to run full scanner across historical artifacts; infra budget request pending (Finance ticket INF-BUD-33). Decision: run incremental runs by week until budget approved.
- Dependency: platform-auth team needs to accept the per-sidecar IAM approach; schedule sync with them next week (Jonah to coordinate).

Open questions to resolve before next sync:
- Do we require rotation of all service-account keys older than 90 days across staging by default? (proposal sounds reasonable; confirm policy)
- Should secrets scanner automatically open JIRA tickets for actionable hits or just tag the repo owners? (platform prefers repo tagging; security prefers tickets for auditability)

Next meeting: Convert to short async update on Slack on 2026-04-27, full sync in-person on 2026-05-04 to review progress on A3/A6/A8.

Notes added: recording link and raw scanner CSV attached to the Confluence page.

End of notes.
